What an on-the-day coordinator actually does

You planned it. Somebody else runs it. This page sets out what happens in each week of the four to six week handover, what goes into a run sheet, what an on the day wedding coordinator does hour by hour, and when this is the wrong thing to buy.

Find a CoordinatorWedding coordinators
  • Handover four to six weeks out
  • Your plan and your suppliers stay as they are
  • Free to enquire

What is on-the-day coordination, and what is it not?

On-the-day coordination is the purchase of a handover. An on the day wedding coordinator takes a finished plan off you four to six weeks before the event, verifies every part of it, writes the one document everybody works from, and runs the day so you are not the person suppliers ring. Nothing you booked changes. The product is transfer of responsibility, not creative input.

It is not planning. A coordinator will not source your caterer, negotiate your venue contract or build your budget, and a package that includes those things is partial planning wearing a coordination price tag. It is not a venue coordinator either, who works for the venue and manages what happens inside it. And despite the name it is not a one day job, which is why some planners sell the same thing as month of coordination or wedding day management rather than day of coordination.

The product exists because planning an event and hosting one are different jobs, and the second cannot be done while you are also the switchboard. On the day coordination is the smallest amount of help that solves the largest problem.

The handover

What happens in each of the six weeks before?

Nobody publishes the handover properly, so here it is in full, week by week. A four week handover compresses weeks six and five into one.

What a coordinator does in each week of a six week handover. Coordinators vary, so confirm the schedule in your contract.
WeekWhat the coordinator doesWhat you do
Six weeks outThe handover meeting. They read every contract, floor plan, invoice and email thread you have, and build a master contact list.Hand over everything, including the unfinished parts.
Five weeks outThe gap report: bookings never confirmed in writing, two suppliers given different arrival times, no wet weather plan, an access window too short for the set.Make the decisions the gap report asks for. The week your involvement matters most.
Four weeks outFirst contact with every supplier, confirming date, arrival time, access route, set up duration, power, meals and pack down.One email introducing the coordinator, so suppliers know who now speaks for you.
Three weeks outThe run sheet is drafted from the confirmations, not your wishes. Conflicts surface here, such as two suppliers wanting the same room at once.Read the draft. The last comfortable point to change the shape of the day.
Two weeks outRun sheet finalised and circulated to every supplier and the venue, with floor plan and set details attached. Contingencies agreed.Confirm final numbers, settle payments and stop adding things.
The last weekFinal confirmation with each supplier, delivery sequence agreed, personal items collected and a decision maker nominated.Hand over the personal items.
The day beforeRehearsal, site check, deliveries received, and the coordinator's kit packed: run sheets, tape, pins, chargers and a printed contact list.Nothing. If you are working the day before, the handover did not happen.

Scroll the table sideways to see every column.

The document

What is actually in a run sheet?

Not a schedule of your day. A schedule of everybody's day, including the eleven people you will never see. These are the sections it needs.

The header block

Date, venue addresses for every site, the coordinator's mobile, the venue contact and the nominated decision maker. If a supplier prints one page, this is it.

The supplier schedule

Every supplier in arrival order, with a time, a contact number, what they deliver and where it goes. This is what prevents three vans in one loading zone.

Bump in and set details

Access route, lift or stair, load limits, where the truck parks and who signs for deliveries. On a dry hire site, the longest section.

The guest-facing timeline

Arrival, formalities, food service, speeches, cake, first dance and carriages, with a person responsible for calling each one.

Formalities and the order of them

Who speaks, in what order, for how long and who is holding the microphone. Speeches are where run sheets most often lose fifteen minutes.

Contacts, in one list

Every supplier, the venue, the celebrant, key family members and anyone with a job. Mobile numbers, not email addresses.

Contingencies

The wet weather call, who makes it and by what time, and what happens if a supplier is late. Nobody invents a good plan at four in the afternoon.

Pack down

What leaves that night, what is collected in the morning, who has keys and who does the final walk through with the venue.

The day

What does the coordinator do hour by hour?

A wedding with a 4pm ceremony and a reception at the same site. The times change for other events. The pattern does not.

On-the-day coordination hour by hour, for a 4pm ceremony and a same site reception.
TimeThe coordinatorYou
7:30amFirst on site. Walks the venue, checks the room against the floor plan and confirms the wet weather call.Breakfast. Not answering your phone.
9:00amReceives the first deliveries. Hire, furniture and infrastructure go in first, because everything else sits on top of them.Hair and makeup.
11:00amStyling and florals arrive. Placement directed against the plan, and the first conflict solved, usually two suppliers wanting the same space.Still not on your phone.
1:00pmCeremony set, chairs counted, signing table checked, music tested, celebrant briefed on timings.Photographs, or the lunch somebody was reminded to provide.
2:30pmReception room finished and photographed for you. Place cards and signage placed, caterer briefed on service timings.Getting dressed.
3:15pmGuest arrival managed, late suppliers chased. The coordinator is the only person holding the whole picture.Waiting, calmly, out of sight.
4:00pmCeremony run. Music cues called, guests seated, the processional started on time because somebody is holding a run sheet.Getting married.
6:00pmRoom flip done, drinks released, guests seated, food service called and the speech order confirmed.Sitting down for the first time.
8:00pmSpeeches and cake called on time. Band or DJ briefed on the first dance and the curfew.Enjoying your own event.
10:30pmPack down begins quietly at the back. Suppliers released in order, gifts and personal items handed to the nominated person.Dancing.
11:45pmLast off site. Final walk through, damages check, keys returned, hire stacked for morning collection.Gone.

Cost

What does on-the-day coordination cost in Australia?

Two Australian sources publish figures and they do not agree, because they describe different handover lengths.

Easy Weddings, in a guide updated February 2026 drawing on its 2025 Wedding Industry Report, puts a day-of coordinator at roughly $1,500 to $2,000. Airtasker's Australian cost guide, updated February 2025, gives a wider $1,000 to $5,000. The gap is handover length and on-site hours, not one source being wrong.

Four things move the price of an on the day wedding coordinator: how early the handover starts, because six weeks of supplier confirmation is far more work than two; whether the ceremony and reception are at the same site, since two sites means travel and usually a second staff member; guest count; and whether the venue is dry hire, because a blank site has a set that must be built rather than turned on. Compare the handover length and the on-site hours before the headline number, because a two week handover with eight hours on site is a different product from six weeks with cover from bump in to pack down.

$1,500 to $2,000

Day-of coordinator range published by Easy Weddings, guide updated February 2026.

$1,000 to $5,000

Day-of coordination range in Airtasker's Australian cost guide, updated February 2025.

4 to 6 weeks

The standard Australian handover window, and the number to compare between two quotes.

The wrong buy

When is on-the-day coordination the wrong choice?

Three situations where an on the day wedding coordinator costs you more than buying the right thing would have.

No. 01

Your plan is not finished

Coordination assumes a complete, confirmed plan handed over intact. If suppliers are unbooked or the budget is not reconciled, a coordinator either declines or reprices as partial planning at short notice, which is the expensive way to buy it.

No. 02

The venue is dry hire and untested

A blank site with no infrastructure and no prior event history is a production job. Somebody has to design the power, the flow and the contingency, and that happens months out, not in a handover.

No. 03

You are inside four weeks

Some coordinators decline inside six weeks and most decline inside four, because the supplier confirmation work cannot be done properly in the time. Ask about a reduced scope explicitly.

Straight answers

Coordination questions

How much does an on the day wedding coordinator cost?

Easy Weddings, in a guide updated February 2026, puts a day-of coordinator at roughly $1,500 to $2,000. Airtasker's Australian guide, updated February 2025, gives $1,000 to $5,000. The difference is mostly the length of the handover, whether the ceremony and reception are at the same site, and how many staff are on the ground.

When does the handover actually start?

Four to six weeks before the event is standard in Australia, which is why day of coordination is a misleading name. Most of the value is delivered in those weeks, in the supplier confirmation and the run sheet. Coordinators are usually booked two to three months out so the handover has room to run.

What is the difference between day of coordination and month of coordination?

Mostly the label. Both describe the same product: a handover of a finished plan, supplier confirmation, a run sheet and on-site management. Month of coordination and wedding day management are simply more honest names, because the work does not begin on the day. Compare the handover length in the contract, not the name on the package.

Do I still need a coordinator if my venue has one?

They do different jobs. A venue coordinator works for the venue and manages what happens inside it. On the day coordination covers your whole event, including suppliers outside the venue contract, a ceremony held somewhere else, and the decisions nobody at the venue is authorised to make. Our wedding coordinators page compares the two roles.

What do I need to hand over at the handover meeting?

Every supplier contract and contact number, all invoices and what is still owing, the venue floor plan and access details, your timings, the seating chart, and an honest list of what you are worried about. Hand over the unfinished parts too.
